common_name_english: Common Asian Toad / Asian Black-spotted Toad
habitat_primary: Terrestrial — urban gardens, drains, vegetation near buildings, road verges
habitat_secondary: Pond/drain edges; temporarily flooded areas for breeding
urban_tolerance: Very High — most urban-adapted amphibian in Dhaka; survives in highly modified environments
bank_vegetation_required: No — breeds in any temporarily flooded pocket
breeding_habitat: Any still or slowly moving water — ditches, garden ponds, drain margins, construction puddles
tadpole_mosquito_predation: Moderate — tadpoles consume Aedes larvae but less efficiently than Euphlyctis or Hoplobatrachus tadpoles
adult_mosquito_predation: Moderate — adult toads consume adult mosquitoes on land but cannot access water-surface larvae
dhaka_wetland_sensitivity: Low — most tolerant species; can persist even in highly urbanised zones
primary_threats_dhaka: Road mortality; toxin poisoning from pesticide runoff; habitat fragmentation reduces gene flow
habitat_suitability_model_role: BASELINE/REFERENCE SPECIES — High urban presence indicates ecological simplification (loss of sensitive predators replaced by generalists)
evidence_of_urban_decline: No significant urban decline observed. Dominates Dhaka records (83/172 = 48%). Its high abundance relative to specialist aquatic species is itself evidence of ecological degradation.
notes_for_research: CRITICAL ARGUMENT: The fact that Duttaphrynus (urban generalist, low predation efficiency) has replaced Hoplobatrachus and Euphlyctis (specialist predators) in Dhaka is an ecological simplification pattern that directly supports your argument about reduced biological control.
